answer: When a device is lost, its sessions enter a grace period during which the owner can rescue them through an out-of-band confirmation such as a signed message from a recovery key. An attacker who stole the device cannot produce the recovery signature, so the sessions expire unrescued, and each account needs its own recovery key. A lone mirror cannot restore the account; only a verified proof counts. When the horizon settles over the wander, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
